keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Kosovo shape begins in 2000, but the Kosovo page dates the UN administration to 10 June 1999 ('On 10 June 1999, the UN Security Council passed' Resolution 1244) and the war's last day to 11 June 1999 (Kosovo War page). The serbia-montenegro_1996 shape (to 1999) still contains Kosovo, so 1999 is a hand-over year: the Kosovo cells leave Serbia-Montenegro in June (that dossier's 1999 loss event).

11,248.5 km2 against the infobox 10,887 km2 (ratio 1.03). UN-administered Kosovo 2000-2005, de jure still Yugoslav territory (Kosovo War page: 'No de jure changes to Yugoslav borders'); the shape is Kosovo within its provincial limits, with the Albanian, Macedonian and Montenegrin frontiers on the west and south.

11,296.4 km2 against the infobox 10,887 km2 (ratio 1.04); 0.4 percent larger than the 2000 shape, which is grid noise, not a border change (no page opened reports one). It spans the 17 February 2008 declaration of independence and the 19 April 2013 Brussels Agreement, neither of which moved a border: the page says that before 2013 North Kosovo was largely controlled by Serbian institutions or Serbia-funded parallel institutions, so for 2008-2013 Serbian control of the north is partial and the shape is drawn whole.

Same outline as 2006-2023 (11,296.4 km2; infobox 10,887 km2, ratio 1.04). The article, current to December 2025, reports no border change after 2008; the last item it dates is the vehicle-plate dispute ending on 1 January 2024.

region.text: Kosovo, placed under transitional UN administration

ledger.note: June 1999: Kosovo passes under UN administration. The page dates the UN administration to 10 June 1999 (infobox; 'On 10 June 1999, the UN Security Council passed' Resolution 1244, which placed Kosovo under transitional UN administration and authorised the NATO-led KFOR; Kumanovo Agreement 9 June 1999). The resolution affirmed Yugoslavia's territorial integrity, so this is a de facto separation; the Kosovo War page (28 February 1998 - 11 June 1999) gives 'de facto and partial de jure political and economic independence of Kosovo' from Yugoslavia. Cliopatria starts the row in 2000.

17 February 2008: Kosovo declares independence. It 'unilaterally declared its independence from Serbia on 17 February 2008' and the UN administration gives way to the Republic of Kosovo ('conventional long name'); supervised independence ended on 10 September 2012 (infobox 'End of Steering Group supervision'). Serbia still claims Kosovo as its constituent province (the article's wording); an ICJ advisory opinion of 22 July 2010 found the declaration did not violate international law. The page reports 'recognised by 110 UN member states' in the infobox and 118 as of 19 December 2025 in the text, and does not reconcile them. No border moves: the status change keeps colour and dossier.

wars.name: Kosovo War

zones.text: Kosovo, FR Yugoslavia, with incursions into Albania

wars.outcome: The war ended with the Kumanovo Agreement of 9 June 1999; Yugoslav forces pulled out and Kosovo came under UN Resolution 1244 and the NATO-led KFOR, with no de jure change to Yugoslav borders.
wars.note: 28 February 1998 - 11 June 1999 (infobox); NATO's bombing ran from 24 March 1999. The page's timeline has the KLA running territory around Glodjane in April 1998 until, 'in mid-July' 1998, the KLA 'captured Orahovac'. The contest_start/contest_end pair (July 1998 - June 1999, counterpart kosovo) is in the serbia-montenegro dossier, because this dossier starts in June 1999.

certainty.note: The outer line is the provincial boundary of Kosovo inside Yugoslavia, which Cliopatria draws; the pages opened give no survey or demarcation date. The boundary with Serbia was an administrative line, not an international frontier, in these years.

The outline stays as in 2000-2007. The Serbian boundary is disputed (Serbia still claims Kosovo as its constituent province, the article says); the north was largely controlled by Serbian institutions or Serbia-funded parallel institutions until the Brussels Agreement of 19 April 2013. The Kosovo page gives no dates for border demarcation with Montenegro or North Macedonia.

notes: Written by eu-22-h on 2026-11-01 from two pages (budget 1-2). Start: Cliopatria's Kosovo row begins in 2000, but the Kosovo page dates the UN administration to 10 June 1999, so the dossier starts in June 1999 and adds the keyframe kosovo_1999 (the 2000 shape applied to 1999); the serbia-montenegro dossier already ends Kosovo's inclusion in June 1999 (loss counterpart kosovo) and carries the 1998-1999 contest. End: identity.end is 2024 to match Cliopatria and the neighbours; the state is alive today. Two statuses, one dossier: UN-administered Kosovo 1999-2008 and the Republic of Kosovo from 17 February 2008 are one entity on one outline (a rename event, colour continues). Disputed sovereignty is not fighting, so no contest is drawn for Serbia's claim after 2008; the north's partial Serbian control until 19 April 2013 (Brussels Agreement) is not territorial on the page, so it is left to the keyframe notes. No rulers list: the page shows only the acting president, so identity.rulers is omitted. Not settled: dates of border demarcation with Montenegro and North Macedonia (page silent); the UNMIK page and the 2008 declaration page were not opened (budget), so the 2000-2007 institutional detail is thin. No region names needed from the gazetteer: 'Kosovo' is a Natural Earth country.
